article_title: SQLite 3.54.0 Adds CLI Prompt Escape Sequences and a .diskused Command, Deprecates sqlite3_analyzer and Requires Windows Vista or Later

content_preview.title: SQLite 3.54.0 Adds CLI Prompt Escape Sequences and a .diskused Command, Deprecates sqlite3_analyzer and Requires Windows Vista or Later
content_preview.summary: SQLite 3.54.0, dated 2026-10-09, reworks the sqlite3 CLI, adds query planner changes and new date modifiers, and ends Windows XP support, per the project's release log.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

SQLite 3.54.0 is dated 2026-10-09 in the project's [release log](https://sqlite.org/releaselog/3_54_0.html). The [SQLite news page](https://sqlite.org/news.html) says the version "includes significant enhancements to the command-line interface (CLI) program" as well as query planner improvements, new features, performance improvements and "countless fixes for AI-discovered bugs". It also ends support for Windows XP and earlier and is the last release to include the `sqlite3_analyzer...

editor_notes.content_quality: News, 863 words (raw and with link URLs stripped; policy range 400-1200). Title 135 characters (cap 150). Clear structure: Overview, CLI changes, planner/SQL/API changes, Windows and performance, What We Don't Know. Vendor claims are attributed to the SQLite release log, news page and documentation. Freshness: release dated 2026-10-09, reviewed 2026-10-13. No internal links (all links are external sqlite.org URLs).
editor_notes.source_verification: All four snapshots exist (source-0..3.html.gz, HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null) and contain page bodies, not just chrome. source-0 (releaselog/3_54_0.html): confirmed every CLI, planner, SQL/API, date, Windows, authorizer, O_TMPFILE and performance item the article lists. Title claims: 'CLI prompt strings may contain escape sequences that expand to show state information' is the exact first CLI item. '.diskused': release log says 'Use the new diskused() extension to implement the ".diskused" dot-command. The replaces the separate sqlite3_analyzer utility program, which is now deprecated.' cli.html section 16: 'The ".diskused" command, which is new as of SQLite 3.54.0 (2026-10-09), outputs human-readable text that shows how much filesystem space is used by the tables and indexes of the main database file ... intended as a replacement for the legacy sqlite3_analyzer command-line utility, which is now deprecated'; output is a CREATE TABLE for 'space_used' with text in a comment; implemented using the diskused() SQL function. 'Deprecates sqlite3_analyzer': the sources do use the word deprecated (release log, cli.html, and news.html 'the stand-alone sqlite3_analyzer program is deprecated'), and news.html also says 'This is the last release that will include the "sqlite3_analyzer" utility program', so the title is accurate, no defect. 'Requires Windows Vista or Later': release log says 'Drop support for WindowsXP and earlier Windows versions, including WindowsCE. SQLite for Windows now requires Windows Vista (circa 2007) or later'; news.html says 'Beginning with this release, SQLite will not compile on Windows version prior to Windows Vista'. This describes the current release, so 'requires' is accurate. Performance: 'About 4% faster, as measured by counting CPU cycles in the speedtest1 preformance benchmark using valgrind on Linux x64. About 7.5% faster compared to one year ago (version 3.51.0).' The 4% figure has no stated baseline in the log; the article says so and attributes both numbers to the project. source-1 (news.html): verbatim quotes 'includes significant enhancements to the command-line interface (CLI) program' and 'countless fixes for AI-discovered bugs' confirmed (the latter split across a line break); 3.53.4 entry dated 2026-07-24 confirmed, including 'huge rush of AI-aided bug reporting' and the 2026-04-09 date of 3.53.0; the remainder of the article's sentence is paraphrase of the declining report rate. source-2 (cli.html): .diskused text as above. source-3 (lang_datefunc.html): 'The "end of" modifiers (19 through 21) shift the date forwards to the last millisecond of the subject month, year, or day'; 'Negative values for the weekday modifier are supported beginning in SQLite version 3.54.0'; N must be between -6 and +6; example SELECT date('2026-01-01','end of year','weekday -5') for the last Friday of 2026. Live re-fetch of the release log via curl returned content byte-identical to the snapshot (sha256 4d165141...), so no edits since capture; live news.html still contains the AI-discovered bugs wording. sqlite.org is already in config/source_allowlist.txt (line 1044); no allowlist change. No suspicious_patterns in the manifest; the only 'injection' text on news.html is unrelated SQL-injection discussion in old news entries, not an instruction aimed at an agent.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics trace to the four sources. The AI-discovered bug fixes are not itemised in the release log or news page; the article states that no CVE or severity is given in these sources and does not call them security fixes, which stays within the sources' wording.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive; vendor measurements explicitly attributed to the SQLite project; no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior SQLite 3.54.0 coverage. An earlier article on SQLite's AI-hallucinated CVE page (2026-08) is linked as a curated related article in the meta file; different angle.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed News article resting entirely on SQLite's own pages, all verified against snapshots and a live re-fetch. Approved without corrections.
